measures: P(reference solve fails | one legal-but-wrong action injected)
control: same injection points with `wait` substituted -- legal, changes nothing, spends one step. `excess_fragility` is fragility minus control, and is the part not explained by simply having spent a step
reading: near 0 is disjunctive -- many solutions, a wrong move is recoverable. near 1 is conjunctive -- one solution, any deviation is fatal
not_measured: whether a policy can find any of those solutions. A disjunctive task can still be unlearnable; read this beside the random floor, not instead of it
solver_restarts: the solver is re-invoked on the perturbed state up to --restarts times, because most reference solvers are straight-line plans and would otherwise score the plan's shape rather than the task's

finding.question: Factorion (github.com/beyarkay/factorion) separates disjunctive tasks -- many solutions, partial progress counts -- from conjunctive ones -- every component simultaneously right or no reward. Does that axis explain why behaviour cloning scores 1.00 on restore_power and 0.13-0.17 on repair_belt?
finding.answer: No. Not supported by this measurement.
finding.why: After the no-op control and the solver restart, excess fragility across five families spans 0.00 to 0.10 -- flat -- while the learning outcomes for those same families span 0.00 to 1.00. Every family measures disjunctive. A measure that does not vary cannot explain an outcome that does.
two_artefacts_this_had_to_survive_first: Without a control, deliver measured the MOST fragile of four families (0.20-0.35) while being the one that learns best, and repair_belt the LEAST (0.00-0.05) while being the one BC fails hardest on. Backwards.

The control located it: every one of deliver's no-op failures was injected at the last action of the solve, always give_iron-plate_20 -- the delivery itself. Replacing the goal-achieving step of a straight-line plan means it is never taken. Re-invoking the solver on the perturbed state (--restarts) dropped deliver from 0.23-0.28 to 0.033-0.08 and its control from 0.20-0.32 to 0.00-0.04.
finding.what_the_number_does_say: The reference solvers are robust rather than brittle scripts: perturbed once with a mask-legal wrong action and re-invoked, they still reach the goal in 96-100% of trials across five families and both splits. That had not been measured before and is worth having on its own -- it is a property of the solvers used to generate every behaviour-cloning dataset in this repository.

an_observation_not_a_result.claim: The one ordering in this data that does track learning outcomes is reference solve length, not solution multiplicity: navigate 9.2 actions, restore_power 14.8, deliver 16.8, repair_belt 21.7, build_line 240.0 -- against outcomes that fall monotonically across the same order (restore_power BC 1.00, deliver PPO 0.89, repair_belt BC 0.15, build_line BC 0.00 on the seeds row).
an_observation_not_a_result.why_it_is_not_being_claimed: n=5, no controlled variation, and horizon is confounded with action-type count and with demonstrations-per-pair. Fitting a second hypothesis to the same five points that falsified the first is how this repository has previously talked itself into findings. Recorded so it can be tested, not asserted.

finding.limits_of_the_instrument: It measures P(reference solver fails | one wrong action), not P(a policy can find any solution). A disjunctive task can still be unlearnable, which is precisely what repair_belt and build_line appear to be. Read beside the random floor from tools/solvability.py, not instead of it.
